name: Peñarol 1960–1966
scopeNote: Peñarol from the first Copa Libertadores 1960 match (19 April 1960, 7-1 v Jorge Wilstermann, RSSSF) to the 1966 Intercontinental Cup second leg (26 October 1966, Madrid, 2-0, 4-0 on points). Two eras of coaching: Roberto Scarone 1960-62 (4-2-4 / 4-4-2 per Trivela) and Roque Máspoli by 1965-66; coaches for 1962-65 not verified in sources read (web search budget ran out before the gap pass). Style named by sources: 4-2-4 / 4-4-2, a team that defended and counterattacked at speed ('nos dejábamos dominar') per a player in El Observador. Tactical coverage is thin and mostly tier C; no zonal/man-marking description of Peñarol itself was found (Spencer's remark on Real Madrid's man-marking is about the opponent). Dates for coach tenures are by year only.
openQuestions: Who coached Peñarol between Scarone's exit (1962 per Trivela) and Máspoli (verified only for 1965 and 1966)? A search summary (not read on a page) named Béla Guttmann in 1962; El Observador mentions Rafael Milans and Oswaldo Brandão only for the 1966-69 unbeaten run. Unverified; the managers[] ends for Scarone and start for Máspoli are approximate.

Possibly two eras: Scarone's side (1960-62, Cubilla, Hohberg, Sasía, Joya, Ledesma) versus Máspoli's 1965-66 side (Mazurkiewicz, Gonçalves, Caetano, Rocha, Abbadie, Figueroa). Spencer is the only constant star.
The El Observador defensive quote (played in Italy 1956-62, returned in 1962) is unnamed in the digest paragraph; speaker not identified, so it covers 1962-66 only loosely.
Gonçalves's 1966 playoff quote (rough play v River Plate) comes from a Wikipedia page quoting El Gráfico, years later.
Pressing, possession, build-up, set-pieces and shape in the Máspoli years have no verified fact; Hugo Bagnulo coached 1958-59 only (outside the period), so excluded from managers[].
Scarone's departure year (1962) comes from a single tier C source; Wikipedia gives 1959-1962 vaguely; no exact day found.

sources.title: Peñarol y el mayor récord de partidos invicto por el Campeonato Uruguayo
sources.evidence: Teníamos un buen equipo. Jugábamos distinto, de atrás para adelante. No atacábamos, pese a los jugadorazos que teníamos. No íbamos a regalarnos, nos dejábamos dominar, que vinieran, porque era muy difícil jugar contra una defensa cerrada. Los contrarios nos decían: 'Contra ustedes no se puede jugar'. ¿Porqué? Porque nos defendíamos y ahora se habla de atacar.

sources.title: Peñarol's golden five-year periods
sources.evidence: In 1958, Gaston Guelfi arrived as president of the club, accompanied by Washington Cataldi and together they would begin a new golden era for the club, bringing in coach Hugo Bagnulo, who had just been coach of the Uruguay national team.

sources.title: Peñarol's golden five-year periods
sources.evidence: In 1959, a Peñarol scout saw an Ecuadorian striker playing with his national team that left him impressed and after Bagnulo's approval, he went to Ecuador to close his signing

sources.title: Peñarol's golden five-year periods
sources.evidence: Bagnulo also led the team to win the 1959 championship, the year in which he left office and was succeeded by Roberto Scarone, with whom Peñarol would win 3 more championships, achieving its first golden five-year period. As a curious fact, the team only lost one match in each season it won between 1960 and 1962.

sources.title: Peñarol's golden five-year periods
sources.evidence: A year later, the black and gold team was reinforced by Joya and Sasia and won the Copa Libertadores again, this time against Palmeiras.
